intake_questions.who_may_book: An adult who owns or rents the home, or a landlord or property manager they name. A renter booking a lawn renovation or a spray may need the owner's OK.

stop: a power line down in the yard
someone swallowed or splashed a lawn chemical
a wasp or hornet nest in the yard
a tree or a big limb down on the house
safety_and_stop_words.go_on: No, for a power line down, a poisoning or a gas smell. Yes, with the area left out, for a nest or a fallen limb in the yard.
stop_action: A power line down: stay well away, keep children and pets inside, treat it as live. Call 911, then the power company. No crew is booked until the utility says it's safe.
A chemical swallowed or splashed: call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222, or 911 if the person isn't breathing or can't wake up. Keep the product label at hand.
A gas smell: leave and call 911. No booking until it's safe.
A wasp or hornet nest: the crew leaves that area out. Pest control can come first.
A tree or limb on the house: call 911 if anyone is hurt; a tree service comes first, then the lawn work.

prep: Keep pets inside, or where you said
Pick up toys, hoses and dog waste
Leave the gate unlocked, or the code on the secure page
Before a spray: close nearby windows, and keep children and pets off the lawn

skills: Sprays and lawn renovation (certified applicator only)
Mower repair at the shop: sharpening, tune-ups, carburetor work
staff.licenses_or_certificates: Each person who sprays holds the state's applicator certification. Where the state allows a registered technician to spray under a certified applicator, the supervision rule comes from its form. Mowing crews and mechanics need none.
staff.who_oks: The owner OKs new mowing customers' prices (he checks the lot) and quotes over the limit. The office manager may too; the owner's answer wins.
staff.crews: Two per mowing or cleanup crew: a lead, who sees the gate code and texts DONE, and a helper.

children_and_age.who_may_book: An adult who owns or rents the home, or a landlord or property manager they name. A renter booking a lawn renovation or a spray may need the owner's OK.
children_and_age.minors_texts: Nobody under 18 books. A teen at home isn't the booking's adult.

visit.check_in: Someone home (the first cut's walk-around, a visit priced on site): the code at the door, entered by the crew lead. Nobody home (plan mows, sprays, aeration, plowing): no code; DONE with a photo of the lawn and the latched gate.
visit.done: Before and after photos, and a photo of the latched gate. A spray adds the application record the state's rules require.
visit.changes_at_visit: Brush clearing is priced before any work. Extra work (beds, a hedge, a leaf haul-away) only when the customer asks, priced first. A right to cancel where the state's rules give one.

license.note: Optional. Upload anything. Rosie never checks it and never shows it as checked (D96).
license.need: Mowing, trimming, leaf cleanup, aeration and snow plowing: usually none. Any weed control, insect control or weed-and-feed done for pay: the state's pesticide business license, and a certified applicator for each spray. Where a town or county licenses landscapers, the state's form says so.
license.who: Both: the company holds the business license, and each person who sprays holds their own certification. Mowing crews need none.
license.ask: The company's pesticide business license number, and each applicator's own certification number and category (turf), where the state's form asks for them.
license.insurance: Where the state's form asks for liability insurance or a bond for the pesticide license, it's asked here. Insured is shown as given by the business, not checked by Rosie.
license.background: Only where the state's rules require them, or as the business's own word.

never_in_a_text: Health reasons for staying away from a product
Neighbors' names or numbers: Rosie never texts the neighbors
languages: English and Spanish. Neighbor notices are printed by the business, in the languages the state's rules ask for.
